claim: Patched (Ptch) is a proton driven antiporter required for Smoothened (Smo) inhibition.
source: Ptch, a proton driven antiporter, is required for Smo inhibition via an unknown mechanism.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a known property of Ptch, supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: Hedgehog (Hh) ligand binding to Patched reverses Smoothened inhibition.
source: Hh ligand binding to Ptch reverses this inhibition and activated Smo initiates the Hh response.
evidence: This is a well-established mechanism in Hedgehog signaling described in the abstract.

claim: Ptch1 and Ptch2 mediate secretion of a Smo-inhibitory cholesterol precursor.
source: These findings support a model in which Ptch1/2 mediate secretion of a Smo-inhibitory cholesterol precursor.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study based on experimental data from mosaic nEBs.

claim: Hedgehog signaling is critically important during embryonic development.
source: Hedgehog (Hh) signaling is critically important during embryonic development and its aberrant regulation is associated with common, lethal birth defects and cancers.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge cited in the introduction.

claim: Aberrant Hedgehog signaling regulation is associated with common, lethal birth defects and cancers.
source: Hedgehog (Hh) signaling is critically important during embryonic development and its aberrant regulation is associated with common, lethal birth defects and cancers.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about the clinical significance of Hh signaling.

claim: Hedgehog signaling has conserved roles as a morphogen and in tissue homeostasis.
source: Conserved roles as a morphogen and in tissue homeostasis make Hh signaling fundamental to most forms of metazoan life (Briscoe and Thérond, 2013; Hooper and Scott, 2005; Ingham and McMahon, 2001).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Smoothened is a putative G-protein-coupled receptor.
source: Smoothened is a putative G-protein-coupled receptor and Ptch has homology to a family of proton-driven antiporters.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the molecular identity of Smoothened.

claim: Patched has homology to a family of proton-driven antiporters.
source: Smoothened is a putative G-protein-coupled receptor and Ptch has homology to a family of proton-driven antiporters.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the molecular identity of Patched.

claim: Patched in its unbound state inhibits Smoothened cell autonomously.
source: (1) Ptch in its unbound state inhibits Smo cell autonomously
evidence: This is part of the prevailing model of Hh signaling described in the introduction.

claim: Uninhibited Smoothened redistributes in the cell and activates transcription of target genes through downstream factors.
source: (3) uninhibited Smo redistributes in the cell and activates transcription of target genes through downstream factors.
evidence: This is part of the established Hh signaling model.

claim: Patched belongs to the Resistance, Nodulation and Division (RND) family of proton-driven, trimeric efflux pumps.
source: Ptch belongs to the Resistance, Nodulation and Division (RND) family of proton-driven, trimeric efflux pumps that are ubiquitously present in all studied organisms (Nikaido and Takatsuka, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: RND family proteins are ubiquitously present in all studied organisms.
source: Ptch belongs to the Resistance, Nodulation and Division (RND) family of proton-driven, trimeric efflux pumps that are ubiquitously present in all studied organisms (Nikaido and Takatsuka, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: RND proteins secrete diverse molecular cargos, including lipophilic and amphiphilic molecules such as antibiotics and sterols.
source: RNDs secrete diverse molecular cargos, including lipophilic and amphiphilic molecules such as antibiotics and sterols.
evidence: This is established knowledge about RND protein function.

claim: RND proteins confer multidrug resistance via antibiotic efflux in Gram-negative bacteria.
source: They are well studied in Gram-negative bacteria, where they confer multidrug resistance via antibiotic efflux (Tseng et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Patched inhibits Smoothened sub-stoichiometrically by regulating the localization of a Smo regulatory molecule.
source: According to prevailing models, Ptch inhibits Smo sub-stoichiometrically rather than through a direct binding relationship, by regulating the localization of a Smo regulatory molecule (Taipale et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: No Smo-regulatory Ptch substrate has been identified.
source: Despite the discovery of exogenous and endogenous molecules capable of regulating Smo, no Smo-regulatory Ptch substrate has been identified (Sharpe et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: The endogenous cargo of Patched is a steroidal molecule.
source: Nevertheless, several observations indicate that the endogenous cargo of Ptch is a steroidal molecule:
evidence: This is inferred from multiple lines of evidence presented in the manuscript.

claim: The plant-derived steroidal alkaloid cyclopamine binds Smoothened and inhibits the Hedgehog response.
source: (1) the plant-derived steroidal alkaloid cyclopamine binds Smo and inhibits the Hh response (Chen et al., 2002a; Incardona et al., 1998);
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Heterologous Patched expression in yeast enhances BODIPY-cholesterol efflux.
source: (2) heterologous Ptch expression in yeast enhances BODIPY-cholesterol efflux (Bidet et al., 2011);
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: The closest prokaryotic homolog of Patched, HpnH, transports bacterial sterols (hopanoids) from the inner to the outer bacterial membrane.
source: (3) the closest prokaryotic homolog of Ptch, HpnH, transports bacterial sterols (hopanoids) from the inner to the outer bacterial membrane (Doughty et al., 2011);
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: 7-dehydroxycholesterol reductase (7DHCR) catalyzes the conversion of 7DHC into cholesterol.
source: (4) 7-dehydroxycholesterol reductase (7DHCR), catalyzes the conversion of 7DHC into cholesterol
evidence: This is established biochemical knowledge.

claim: Genetic loss of 7dhcr is associated with defects in Shh signaling, perhaps via accumulation of a late sterol precursor (or its derivative) that inhibits Smoothened.
source: genetic loss of 7dhcr is associated with defects in Shh signaling, perhaps via accumulation of a late sterol precursor (or its derivative) that inhibits Smo (Bijlsma et al., 2006; Cohen, 2010; Gruchy et al., 2014; Incardona et al., 2000a; Linder et al., 2015; Sever et al., 2016);
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Patched has a sterol-sensing domain (SSD) that is conserved within sterol biogenesis regulatory enzymes.
source: (5) Ptch has a sterol-sensing domain (SSD) that is conserved within sterol biogenesis regulatory enzymes, and thus likely binds sterols (Incardona, 2005)
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: The sterol-sensing domain of Patched is necessary for Smoothened inhibition in Drosophila.
source: and this domain is necessary for Smo inhibition by Ptch in Drosophila (Strutt et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: A universally conserved Aspartic acid residue in the third transmembrane domain of the SSD is required for transport in bacterial RNDs.
source: Within the third transmembrane domain of the SSD (the fourth transmembrane domain of Ptch1) resides a universally conserved Aspartic acid residue that when mutated in bacterial RNDs blocks transport (Zgurskaya and Nikaido, 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Mutation of the conserved Aspartic acid residue in Patched1 yields an allele unable to inhibit Smoothened both in vivo and in vitro.
source: Mutation of this residue in Ptch1 yields an allele unable to inhibit Smo both in vivo and in vitro (Alfaro et al., 2014; Strutt et al., 2001; Taipale et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Patched1/2 re-localizes a cholesterol precursor that is inhibitory to Smoothened.
source: These observations have led to the hypothesis that Ptch1/2 re-localizes a cholesterol precursor that is inhibitory to Smo (Incardona et al., 1998).
evidence: This is a hypothesis supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Murine fibroblasts overexpressing Patched1 can condition their supernatant with a Smoothened inhibitor.
source: The observation that murine fibroblasts overexpressing Ptch1 can condition their supernatant with a Smo inhibitor supports this notion (Bijlsma et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Patched can sequester Hedgehog ligands from the environment and thus suppress the Hedgehog response.
source: This may be due to other non-cell autonomous mechanisms of Ptch-mediated inhibition unrelated to its antiporter activity, such as its proposed ability to sequester Hedgehog ligands from the environment and thus suppress the Hh response (Chen and Struhl, 1996; Incardona et al., 2000b; Milenkovic et al., 1999; Strutt et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Patched plays a cell autonomous role in the activation of Smoothened via the accumulation of phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate.
source: Besides these possible non-cell autonomous activities, Ptch plays a cell autonomous role in the activation of Smo via the accumulation of phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate (Jiang et al., 2016; Yavari et al., 2010) that can activate Smo via its intracellular C-terminal domain.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Sonic Hedgehog patterns the embryonic vertebrate neural tube through a well-studied transcriptional response.
source: As a morphogen, Sonic Hedgehog (Shh) patterns the embryonic vertebrate neural tube through a well-studied transcriptional response (Cohen et al., 2013; Roelink et al., 1994).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Shh is expressed ventrally in embryos in the notochord and floor plate, yielding a ventral to dorsal gradient of Hedgehog pathway activity.
source: Shh is expressed ventrally in embryos in the notochord and floor plate, yielding a ventral to dorsal gradient of Hh pathway activity in which ventral cell types have a high level of pathway activation.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Shh expression and activity patterns.

claim: Neuralized embryoid bodies (nEBs) are highly responsive to Shh, the Smoothened agonist SAG, and cyclopamine.
source: nEBs have previously been shown to be highly responsive to Shh, the Smo agonist SAG, and cyclopamine, indicating that Smo activity is subject to regulation in this system (Frank-Kamenetsky et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Smoothened becomes maximally activated in nEBs lacking Ptch1 and Ptch2.
source: We have also found that Smo becomes maximally activated in nEBs lacking Ptch1 and Ptch2 (Alfaro et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- nEBs have little Hedgehog pathway activity and high dorsal identity, as indicated by a gain of dorsal Pax7+ cells to levels greater than wild type.
source: For example, Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- mESCs yielded nEBs with little Hh pathway activity and thus high dorsal identity, as indicated by a gain of dorsal Pax7+ cells to levels greater than wild type (Figure 1A,B,J,K).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Ptch1LacZ/LacZ nEBs are highly ventral.
source: Ptch1LacZ/LacZ nEBs by contrast were highly ventral (Figure 1D,M)
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Ptch1LacZ is an established null allele.
source: (Ptch1LacZ is an established null allele [Goodrich et al., 1997; Rohatgi et al., 2007]).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Shh signaling through Ptch2 occurs in cells null for Ptch1.
source: Shh signaling through Ptch2 in cells null for Ptch1 has also been observed
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior observations.

claim: Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Shh-/- nEBs had reduced numbers of Nkx2.2+/Olig2+ cells compared to Ptch1LacZ/LacZ nEBs, indicating ligand dependency of the response.
source: and thus unsurprisingly Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Shh-/- nEBs had reduced numbers of Nkx2.2+/Olig2+ cells (Figure 1E,N), compared to Ptch1LacZ/LacZ nEBs, indicating ligand dependency of the response.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/- nEBs differentiate into identities associated with high Hedgehog pathway activity, indicated by robust Nkx2.2, Isl1/2 and Olig2 expression.
source: As previously reported, Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/- nEBs differentiated into identities associated with high Hh pathway activity, indicated by robust Nkx2.2, Isl1/2 and Olig2 expression (Figure 1G,P) (Alfaro et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1 and citation to prior work.

claim: Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- nEBs had unaffected ventral identity, consistent with Shh-independent Hedgehog pathway activation in the dual absence of Ptch1/2.
source: Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- nEBs had unaffected ventral identity (Figure 1H,Q), consistent with a model for Shh-independent Hh pathway activation in the dual absence of Ptch1/2.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Smoothened is invariably required for the activation of the Hedgehog pathway.
source: Smo was invariably required for the activation of the Hh pathway, as established models predict.
evidence: This is consistent with established models of Hh signaling.

claim: Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Smo-/- and Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Smo-/- nEBs were entirely lacking Nkx2.2, Isl1/2 and Olig2 expression and instead expressed Pax7.
source: Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Smo-/- and Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Smo-/- nEBs were entirely lacking Nkx2.2, Isl1/2 and Olig2 expression and instead expressed Pax7, as did Smo-/- nEBs (Figure 1C,F,I,L,O,R).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: All Smoothened-/- nEBs acquired highly dorsal fates as cells refractory to Shh pathway activation.
source: All Smo-/- nEBs thus conformed to the standard signaling model by acquiring highly dorsal fates as cells refractory to Shh pathway activation.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing Pax7 expression in Smo-/- nEBs.

claim: Each clone had abundant Pax6+ nuclei and Tuj1 expression, suggesting robust neuralization.
source: Each clone had abundant Pax6+ nuclei and Tuj1 expression, suggesting robust neuralization (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Cyclopamine inhibits Isl1/2 and Nkx2.2 expression in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- nEBs with an IC50 around 25 nM.
source: First, we treated nEBs with the Smo inhibitor cyclopamine (Cooper et al., 1998; Gaffield et al., 1999; Incardona et al., 2000a) and found that cyclopamine inhibited Isl1/2 and Nkx2.2 expression with an IC50 around 25 nM (Figure 1S).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1S.

claim: ShhN induces the Hedgehog response in Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- and Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Shh-/- nEBs but not in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- nEBs.
source: We found that ShhN (soluble N-terminal Shh) was able to induce the Hh response both in Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- and Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Shh-/- nEBs but not in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- nEBs, (Figure 1T)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1T.

claim: Ptch1-/- cells respond to Shh via Ptch2.
source: corroborating our report that Ptch1-/- cells respond to Shh via Ptch2 (Alfaro et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/- fibroblasts co-transfected with Gli:Luciferase and Ptch1, then co-cultured with ShhN-transfected cells, activate the Hedgehog response.
source: Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/- fibroblasts co-transfected with Gli:Luciferase, a Hh pathway reporter (Taipale et al., 2000) and Ptch1, then co-cultured with ShhN-transfected cells, activate the Hh response (Figure 1U).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1U.

claim: ShhN alone is unable to activate the Hedgehog pathway in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/- cells.
source: ShhN alone was unable to activate the Hh pathway in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/- cells, consistent with results obtained with nEBs (Figure 1T).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1T.

claim: The ability to respond to exogenous ShhN is lost in the absence of Ptch1/2, but can be restored with Ptch1 transfection.
source: Thus, the ability to respond to exogenous ShhN is lost in the absence of Ptch1/2, but can be restored with Ptch1 transfection.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing restoration of Shh response upon Ptch1 transfection.

claim: Mosaic nEBs comprised 1:1 of Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- and Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells resembled Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- nEBs in their near complete absence of Nkx2.2+ cells.
source: Interestingly, mosaic nEBs comprised 1:1 of the two cell lines resembled Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- nEBs as judged by their near complete absence of Nkx2.2+ cells, and had fewer Olig2+ cells than expected for a 1:1 mosaic.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from mosaic nEBs.

claim: Mosaic nEBs comprised 1:1 of Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- and Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells had fewer Olig2+ cells than expected for a 1:1 mosaic.
source: Interestingly, mosaic nEBs comprised 1:1 of the two cell lines resembled Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- nEBs as judged by their near complete absence of Nkx2.2+ cells, and had fewer Olig2+ cells than expected for a 1:1 mosaic.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from mosaic nEBs.

claim: The reduced Nkx2.2+ and Olig2+ cells in mosaic nEBs is consistent with extracellular flux of Ptch1/2 substrates from Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- cells.
source: Because Shh is genetically absent from these nEBs and Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- mESCs are ligand insensitive, we interpreted this result as consistent with extracellular flux of Ptch1/2 substrates from Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- mESCs in which Ptch1/2 are intact, and inconsistent with Shh sequestration from this compartment of cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Co-culture of Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells with Smo-/- cells significantly decreased Nkx2.2+ cells and increased Olig2+ cells.
source: In contrast, co-culture of Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells with Smo-/- cells significantly decreased Nkx2.2+ cells and increased Olig2+ cells, rejecting the null hypothesis.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from mosaic nEBs.

claim: The changes in Nkx2.2+ and Olig2+ cells in mosaic nEBs represent a dorsal shift in the identity of the Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cell compartment.
source: We interpret this as a dorsal shift in the identity of the Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cell compartment, as Nkx2.2 is a marker of a more ventral neural progenitor domain than Olig2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Ptch1:LacZ levels were low in Ptch1+/LacZ and Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- nEBs but robust in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ and Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/- nEBs at 72 hr.
source: At 72 hr, Ptch1:LacZ levels were low in Ptch1+/LacZ and Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- nEBs but robust in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ and Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/- nEBs (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Ptch1:LacZ levels were reduced in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Shh-/- nEBs but remained elevated in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- nEBs.
source: Ptch1:LacZ levels were reduced in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Shh-/- nEBs but remained elevated in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- nEBs.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claim: Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Smo-/- and Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Smo-/- nEBs had reduced Ptch:LacZ despite Ptch1/2 loss.
source: Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Smo-/- Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Smo-/- nEBs had reduced Ptch:LacZ despite Ptch1/2 loss.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claim: Ptch1:LacZ is a reliable output for Hedgehog pathway activity across cell lines.
source: These data suggest that Ptch1:LacZ is a reliable output for Hh pathway activity across cell lines.
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between Ptch1:LacZ levels and neural progenitor markers.

claim: Ptch1:LacZ was strongly induced in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- nEBs after 72 hr differentiation.
source: We found that Ptch1:LacZ was strongly induced in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- nEBs after 72 hr differentiation (Figure 3C), and this high level of expression persisted for several days.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Ptch1:LacZ expression is suppressed after treatment with cyclopamine, indicating that Ptch1:LacZ upregulation requires Smoothened.
source: Ptch1:LacZ expression is suppressed after treatment with cyclopamine, indicating that Ptch1:LacZ upregulation requires Smo (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Disp1-/-;Ptch1-/-;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- nEBs have robust ventral neural progenitor identity.
source: We observed robust ventral neural progenitor identity only in Disp1-/-;Ptch1-/-;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- nEBs
evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claim: Disp1-/-;Shh-/- and Disp1-/-;Ptch1-/-;Shh-/- nEBs had widespread Pax7+ progenitors, indicating a low level of Hedgehog pathway activation.
source: By contrast Disp1-/-;Shh-/- and Disp1-/-;Ptch1-/-;Shh-/- had widespread Pax7+ progenitors, indicating a low level of Hh pathway activation (Figure 3D–I).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D-I.

claim: Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- nEBs mosaic 1:1 with Disp1-/-;Shh-/-;Ptch1-/-;Ptch2-/- cells yielded Ptch1:LacZ signal closely reflecting the relative mESC contribution of Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells.
source: Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- nEBs mosaic 1:1 with Disp1-/-;Shh-/-;Ptch1-/-;Ptch2-/- cells yielded Ptch1:LacZ signal closely reflecting the relative mESC contribution of Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claim: When Disp1-/-;Shh-/- or Disp1-/-;Shh-/-;Ptch1-/- cells were co-cultured with Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells, Ptch1:LacZ levels in the Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells significantly declined.
source: However, when Disp1-/-;Shh-/- or Disp1-/-;Shh-/-;Ptch1-/- cells were co-cultured with Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells, Ptch1:LacZ levels in the Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells significantly declined (Figure 3J).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3J.

claim: Only small differences were found in Ptch1:LacZ signal derived from Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Smo-/- mESCs co-cultured 1:1 with Disp1-/-;Shh-/-, Disp1-/-;Shh-/-;Ptch1-/- or Disp1-/-;Shh-/-;Ptch1-/-;Ptch2-/- cells.
source: By contrast, only small differences were found in Ptch1:LacZ signal derived from Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Smo-/- mESCs co-cultured 1:1 with Disp1-/-;Shh-/-, Disp1-/-;Shh-/-;Ptch1-/- or Disp1-/-;Shh-/-;Ptch1-/-;Ptch2-/- cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claim: Smoothened is the target of the inhibitory cargo of Ptch1/2 activity.
source: This supports the notion that Smo is the target of the inhibitory cargo of Ptch1/2 activity.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Smo-/- cells do not show changes in Ptch1:LacZ in mosaic nEBs.

claim: Changes in LacZ levels in mosaic nEBs are not attributable to disparities in cell growth or adhesion during the culture period.
source: Labeling the two cell compartments using Cell Tracker dyes, and assessing the resulting mosaic nEBs showed equivalent relative contributions after 48 hr (Figure 3K), indicating that changes in LacZ levels in mosaic nEBs are not attributable to disparities in cell growth or adhesion during the culture period.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3K.

claim: Endogenous Ptch1/2 suppress the Hedgehog response non-cell autonomously in cells lacking Ptch1/2 activity.
source: These results suggest that endogenous Ptch1/2 suppress the Hh response non-cell autonomously in cells lacking Ptch1/2 activity.
evidence: This is the main conclusion inferred from the mosaic nEB experiments.

claim: Significantly less Ptch1:LacZ signal was obtained from nEBs containing Shh-/-;7dhcr-/- cells as compared with nEBs containing parental Shh-/- cells.
source: Significantly less Ptch1:LacZ signal was obtained from nEBs containing Shh-/-;7dhcr-/- cells as compared with nEBs containing parental Shh-/- cells (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: nEBs are cultured in a cholesterol-free environment and likely upregulate cholesterol synthesis.
source: Because nEBs are cultured in a cholesterol-free environment, they likely upregulate cholesterol synthesis (Brown and Goldstein, 1986).
evidence: This is inferred from established knowledge about cholesterol regulation and citation to prior literature.

claim: Accumulation of 7DHC, or a 7DHC derivative, in Shh-/-;7dhcr-/- cells may provide a larger pool of the Ptch1/2 cargo, increasing secretion of the Smo-inhibitory sterol.
source: Accumulation of 7DHC, or a 7DHC derivative (Bijlsma et al., 2006; Sever et al., 2016) in Shh-/-;7dhcr-/- cells may thus provide a larger pool of the Ptch1/2 cargo, increasing secretion of the Smo-inhibitory sterol, possibly 7DHC.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: A decreased Hedgehog response was observed in nEBs treated with 7DHC compared to control treatment with cholesterol.
source: Corroborating earlier findings (Bijlsma et al., 2006), we observed a decreased Hh response in nEBs treated with 7DHC compared to control treatment with cholesterol, regardless of whether the nEB was mosaic or comprised exclusively of Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C and citation to prior literature.

claim: A larger inhibition of the Hedgehog response by exogenous 7DHC was observed in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells co-cultured 1:1 in nEBs with Shh-/- as opposed to Shh-/-;7dhcr-/- cells.
source: We additionally saw differences between the mosaic nEBs. A larger inhibition of the Hh response by exogenous 7DHC was observed in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells co-cultured 1:1 in nEBs with Shh-/- as opposed to Shh-/-;7dhcr-/- cells (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Cells containing Ptch1/2 may be able to process or transport exogenous 7DHC into a more potent non-cell autonomous inhibitor of the Hedgehog response in neighboring Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells.
source: We speculate that cells containing Ptch1/2 may be able to process or transport exogenous 7DHC into a more potent non-cell autonomous inhibitor of the Hh response in neighboring Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: The findings are consistent with Ptch1/2 antiporter activity mediating secretion of 7DHC, or an oxysterol derivative like 3β,5α-dihydroxycholest-7-en-6-one, as a mechanism to inhibit Smoothened in neighboring cells.
source: These findings are consistent with Ptch1/2 antiporter activity mediating secretion of 7DHC, or an oxysterol derivative like 3β,5α-dihydroxycholest-7-en-6-one (Sever et al., 2016), as a mechanism to inhibit Smo in neighboring cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data with citation to prior literature.

claim: Motor neurons arise from a population of neural progenitors in the ventral neural tube, and Hedgehog pathway activation is required for motor neuron differentiation in vivo as well as in nEBs.
source: Motor neurons arise from a population of neural progenitors in the ventral neural tube, and Hh pathway activation is required for motor neuron differentiation in vivo as well as in nEBs.
evidence: This is established knowledge about motor neuron development.

claim: HB9:GFP+ cells had motor neuron morphology and co-labeled with Isl1/2 immunostain.
source: HB9:GFP+ cells had motor neuron morphology and co-labeled with Isl1/2 immunostain, and thus serve as a measure for motor neuron induction (Figure 5B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: A small but significant increase in HB9:GFP+ motor neurons was observed when HB9:GFP cells were co-cultured with Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells as compared to Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- or Ptch1LacZ/-;Shh-/- cells.
source: We observed a small but significant increase in HB9:GFP+motor neurons when these cells were co-cultured with Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells as compared to Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- or Ptch1LacZ/-;Shh-/- cells (Figure 5A,C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A,C.

claim: 10 nM and 100 nM SAG induces motor neuron differentiation in HB9:GFP cells under all mosaic conditions.
source: As predicted, 10 nM and 100 nM SAG induces motor neuron differentiation in HB9:GFP cells under all mosaic conditions (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: A strong synergistic effect was observed between Ptch1/2 loss in surrounding cells and SAG-induced motor neuron differentiation in HB9:GFP cells.
source: However, a strong synergistic effect was observed between Ptch1/2 loss in surrounding cells and SAG-induced motor neuron differentiation in HB9:GFP cells (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A,B.

claim: Compared to Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells, Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- cells suppressed motor neuron induction at both SAG concentrations.
source: We found that compared to Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells, Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- cells suppressed motor neuron induction at both SAG concentrations
evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claim: Ptch1LacZ/-;Shh-/- cells suppressed motor neuron induction to an intermediate degree, presumably via Ptch2 activity.
source: while Ptch1LacZ/-;Shh-/- cells also suppressed motor neuron induction to an intermediate degree (presumably via Ptch2 activity).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and inference about Ptch2 activity.

claim: The observation of synergistic effects between Ptch1/2 loss and SAG is consistent with Ptch1/2 cargo acting as a SAG antagonist.
source: This observation is consistent with Ptch1/2 cargo acting as a SAG antagonist and is not easily reconciled with impaired Hh ligand sequestration due to the lack of Ptch1/2 in the environment, as this scenario should have little effect on SAG-mediated Smo activation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Three-part mosaic nEBs consisting of 94% Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Shh-/- or Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells facilitated robust Shh-mediated HB9:GFP+ motor neuron induction.
source: Three-part mosaic nEBs consisting of 94% Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Shh-/- or Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells facilitated robust Shh-mediated HB9:GFP+ motor neuron induction.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claim: Negligible GFP expression was observed in mosaic nEBs principally comprised of Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- cells.
source: In contrast, we observed negligible GFP expression in mosaic nEBs principally comprised of Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- cells (Figure 6A,D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A,D.

claim: HB9:GFP+ motor neurons were not observed when Shh overexpressing cells were omitted.
source: HB9:GFP+ motor neurons were not observed when Shh overexpressing cells were omitted.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claim: The response to Shh is strongly enhanced by Ptch1/2 absence in nearby cells.
source: Thus, the response to Shh is strongly enhanced by Ptch1/2 absence in nearby cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing enhanced motor neuron induction.

claim: No difference in extracellular Shh staining was found in various mosaic nEBs.
source: We found no difference in extracellular Shh staining in various mosaic nEBs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), further supporting the idea that non-cell autonomous inhibition by Ptch1/2 of the Hh response does not involve Shh sequestration.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Shh robustly induced HB9:GFP+ motor neurons in nEBs consisting of 94% Disp1-/-;Ptch1-/-;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells.
source: Shh robustly induced HB9:GFP+ motor neurons in nEBs consisting of 94% Disp1-/-;Ptch1-/-;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells
evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claim: Motor neuron induction was negligible in nEBs primarily consisting of 94% Disp1-/-;Ptch1-/-;Shh-/- and Disp1-/-;Shh-/- cells.
source: while motor neuron induction was negligible in nEBs primarily consisting of 94% Disp1-/-;Ptch1-/-;Shh-/- and Disp1-/-;Shh-/- cells (Figure 6B,D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B,D.

claim: HB9:GFP+ motor neurons were induced efficiently only in predominantly Ptch1-/-;Ptch2-/-;Smo-/- nEBs.
source: HB9:GFP+ motor neurons were induced efficiently only in predominantly Ptch1-/-;Ptch2-/-;Smo-/- nEBs (Figure 6C,D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C,D.

claim: In nEBs largely comprised of Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells, even a minor fraction of Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- cells suppressed motor neuron induction.
source: In nEBs largely comprised of Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells, even a minor fraction of Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- cells suppressed motor neuron induction (Figure 6E,F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6E,F.

claim: The properties of Ptch1/2 containing cells are dominant over those of cells lacking Ptch1/2 function.
source: This indicates that the properties of Ptch1/2 containing cells are dominant over those of cells lacking Ptch1/2 function, further supporting the notion that Ptch1/2 function mediates the secretion of a Smo inhibitor that de-sensitizes cells to the effects of Shh.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing dominant inhibitory effects.

claim: Ptch1/2 mediate the secretion of a Smoothened inhibitor that affects the Hedgehog response both cell autonomously and in nearby cells.
source: A logical interpretation of these results is that Ptch1/2 mediate the secretion of a Smo inhibitor that affects the Hh response both cell autonomously, and in nearby cells.
evidence: This is the main conclusion inferred from all the experimental data.

claim: Observations similar to the current study but using overexpressed Ptch1 have been reported in fibroblasts.
source: Observations similar to ours but using overexpressed Ptch1 have been reported in fibroblasts and our experiments support this finding (Bijlsma et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Detecting non-cell autonomous activities of Ptch1/2 expressed at endogenous levels in nEBs resolves the argument that overexpressed Ptch1/2 constructs could have non-physiological effects.
source: Detecting these activities of Ptch1/2 expressed at endogenous levels in nEBs resolves the argument that overexpressed Ptch1/2 constructs could have non-physiological effects.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the significance of the current findings.

claim: Cells with a dorsal identity (Disp1-/-;Ptch1-/-;Shh-/-) are better non-cell autonomous repressors of the Hedgehog response than cells with a more ventral identity (Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Shh-/-).
source: Notably, cells with a dorsal identity (Disp1-/-;Ptch1-/-;Shh-/-) are better non-cell autonomous repressors of the Hh response than cells with a more ventral identity (Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Shh-/-).
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data.

claim: The variation in non-cell autonomous repression by Ptch1-/- lines is speculated to be due to varying levels of Ptch2 activity.
source: We speculate that this is due to varying levels of Ptch2 activity.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observed variation.

claim: The loss of Smoothened decreases the ability of Ptch1/2 to inhibit the Hedgehog response non-cell autonomously.
source: It also appears that the loss of Smo decreases the ability of Ptch1/2 to inhibit the Hh response non-cell autonomously.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data.

claim: The decrease in non-cell autonomous inhibition by Ptch1/2 upon Smoothened loss is easily explained by a decrease in Ptch1/2 levels as Ptch1/2 expression is under the control of Smoothened.
source: This observation is easily explained by a decrease in Ptch1/2 levels as Ptch1/2 expression is under the control of Smo.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on established knowledge of Hh pathway regulation.

claim: Even in the complete absence of Hedgehog pathway activation, Ptch1/2 can still inhibit Smoothened.
source: Thus, even in the complete absence of Hh pathway activation, Ptch1/2 can still inhibit Smo.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Ptch1/2 inhibit Smo in Smo-/- cells.

claim: In tissues without detectable levels of Ptch1/2, Smoothened remains inactive.
source: This is consistent with the observation that in tissues without detectable levels of Ptch1/2, Smo remains inactive.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Smo regulation.

claim: Ptch1 localizes to late endosomes while mediating Shh uptake.
source: We previously demonstrated that Ptch1 localizes to late endosomes while mediating Shh uptake, and that Shh signaling requires endosomal acidification (Incardona et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: Shh signaling requires endosomal acidification.
source: We previously demonstrated that Ptch1 localizes to late endosomes while mediating Shh uptake, and that Shh signaling requires endosomal acidification (Incardona et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: Conserved acidic residues required for proton flux in prokaryotic RNDs are also required for Ptch1 to repress Smoothened.
source: Conserved acidic residues required for proton flux in prokaryotic RNDs are also required for Ptch1 to repress Smo (Alfaro et al., 2014; Strutt et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Ptch1/2 may enrich the endosomal lumen or intraluminal vesicular in multivesicular endosomes (MVEs) with a Smoothened inhibitor.
source: One possibility is that Ptch1/2 enrich the endosomal lumen or intraluminal vesicular in multivesicular endosomes (MVEs) with a Smo inhibitor.
evidence: This is a speculative model proposed by the authors.

claim: Exosomal release would allow the Smoothened inhibitor to enter the extracellular environment and regulate Smoothened both cell autonomously as well as non-cell autonomously.
source: Exosomal release would allow this inhibitor to enter the extracellular environment and regulate Smo both cell autonomously as well as non-cell autonomously.
evidence: This is a speculative model proposed by the authors.

claim: Cells enriched in sterol precursors are better non-cell autonomous inhibitors of the Hedgehog response.
source: Our observation that cells enriched in sterol precursors are better cell non-cell autonomous inhibitors of the Hh response complements earlier observations implicating sterols as the Smo inhibitors transported by Ptch1/2.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from 7dhcr-/- cells.

claim: Ptch1/2 become more effective non-cell autonomous inhibitors of Smoothened in nearby cells when expressed in cells enriched for 7DHC or its derivatives.
source: The observation that 7DHCR loss coincides with reduced Hh signaling is refined by our results showing that Ptch1/2 become more effective non-cell autonomous inhibitors of Smo in nearby cells when expressed in cells enriched for 7DHC or its derivatives.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from 7dhcr-/- cells.

claim: 7DHC becomes a more potent inhibitor when acted upon by Ptch1/2 activity.
source: However, our results show that 7DHC becomes a more potent inhibitor when acted upon by Ptch1/2 activity
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing enhanced inhibition in mosaic nEBs.

claim: It is plausible that the Ptch1/2 cargo becomes inhibitory after translocation or secretion.
source: and when combined with the evidence that Ptch1/2 function as proton-driven antiporters, it becomes plausible that the Ptch1/2 cargo becomes inhibitory after translocation or secretion.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation combining multiple lines of evidence.

claim: Ptch1/2 disruption enhances not only cell autonomous Hedgehog responses, but also Smoothened activation in adjacent cells with intact Ptch1/2 activity.
source: an important ramification of our findings is that Ptch1/2 disruption enhances not only cell autonomous Hh responses, but also Smo activation in adjacent cells with intact Ptch1/2 activity (Barakat et al., 2010).
evidence: This is an implication of the findings with citation to prior literature.

claim: Genetically normal stromal cells respond to Shh expressing tumors by infiltrating and supporting them.
source: The finding that genetically normal stromal cells respond to Shh expressing tumors by infiltrating and supporting them heightens the importance of our observations because Ptch1/2 loss in the tumor may affect Shh sensitivity in supporting stromal cells non-cell autonomously (Yauch et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Even in the absence of Ptch1/2, cells remain sensitive to Hedgehog ligands signaling in nearby cells.
source: Our results also predict that even in the absence of Ptch1/2, cells remain sensitive to Hh ligands signaling in nearby cells.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the experimental findings.

claim: Anticancer strategies based on ligand sequestration or inactivation remain viable treatment options.
source: Anticancer strategies based on ligand sequestration or inactivation therefore remain viable treatment options.
evidence: This is an implication of the findings for cancer therapy.

claim: Hedgehog signaling induces Ptch1/2 expression.
source: Invariably, Hh signaling induces Ptch1/2 expression (Holtz et al., 2013)
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Ptch1/2 induction leads to negative feedback, possibly by secreting more Smoothened inhibitor, increasing Shh sequestration, or both.
source: and Ptch1/2 induction then leads to negative feedback, possibly by secreting more Smo inhibitor, increasing Shh sequestration, or both.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the role of Ptch1/2 induction.

claim: The non-cell autonomous inhibition mediated by Ptch1/2 is mediated by the antiporter activity of Ptch1/2, rather than by ligand sequestration.
source: Our finding that Ptch1/2 inhibit the Hh response non-cell autonomously, even in nEBs devoid of Shh ligand, supports the notion that the non-cell autonomous inhibition mediated by Ptch1/2 is mediated by the antiporter activity of Ptch1/2, rather than by ligand sequestration.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data in Shh-/- nEBs.

claim: The ability of relatively few Ptch1/2 expressing cells to inhibit the Hedgehog response supports the idea that non-cell autonomous inhibition is mediated by antiporter activity.
source: The ability of relatively few Ptch1/2 expressing cells to inhibit the Hh response pathway further supports this idea.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing dominant inhibitory effects.

claim: Ptch1/2 act broadly and communally to inhibit Smoothened in tissues undergoing patterning.
source: Together these findings indicate that Ptch1/2 act broadly and communally inhibit Smo in tissues undergoing patterning.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from all the experimental findings.

claim: Local sensitivity to Shh is highly buffered and equalized between cells, aiding the formation of a smooth response gradient in the Shh morphogenetic field.
source: According to this model, local sensitivity to Shh is highly buffered and equalized between cells, aiding the formation of a smooth response gradient in the Shh morphogenetic field.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the findings.
